newsitem.title: USA: Disney posts $333 million profit for quarter.
newsitem.headline: Disney posts $333 million profit for quarter.

text.p: Walt Disney Co. Wednesday reported better-than-expected second quarter profits, reflecting strong theme park attendance and successful films such as Academy Award winner "The English Patient".

The Burbank, Calif.-based entertainment giant earned $333 million or 49 cents a share in the three months ended in March, up from $268 million or 47 cents a share in the year-ago quarter. The year ago period excluded two, one-time charges. Including the charges, Disney had a loss of $25 million, or 4 cents a share in the year-earlier quarter.
Revenues rose 21 percent to $5.48 billion, buoyed by strong results from Disney's film, television and theme park businesses.

The second quarter profit was 5 percent above the First Call consensus estimate of 45 cents a share, sending Disney shares rising to a new 52-week high of $79.625, up $1.375 on the New York Stock Exchange. The stock ended up 87.5 cents at $79.125 in consolidated trading.

Jessica Reif, an entertainment analyst at Merrill Lynch, said the second quarter "was incredibly strong", led by stronger-than-expected results at Disney's theme parks and solid performances at the box office office.

"The film division is starting to see the benefits of some of these Pay-TV channels in Europe and Latin America," she said, referring to recent deals Disney signed to sell films to international television markets. "This is going to affect all of the studios, not just Disney."
Creative Content, which includes Disney's film and music operations, publishing and retail businesses, reported a 9 percent rise in revenues for the quarter and a 56 percent jump in operating income.
Disney benefited from strong box office receipts for the Mel Gibson thriller, "Ransom", the live action adaptation of "101 Dalmatians" and "The English Patient."

"The English Patient," a romantic tale set against the backdrop of World War II, grabbed nine Oscars this year, including best picture and best director. The film was distributed by Disney's Miramax unit.
Disney said its film and music results also were aided by the home video success of "Toy Story" and "The Hunchback of Notre Dame" worldwide and "Bambi" domestically.
Broadcasting revenues rose 9 percent for the quarter to $1.5 billion and operating income increased 18 percent to $238 million.

Disney attributed the improvement to significant reductions in programme amortization and other costs attributable to the Capital Cities/ABC Inc. acquisition, primarily at the television network, which were partially offset by lower network ratings.
The division also benefited from strong cable results driven by increased advertising revenues and subscribers at the all-sports network ESPN and increased subscribers at The Disney Channel.
Strong attendance and higher spending at Disney's theme parks contributed to a 14 percent increase in Theme Parks and Resorts revenues for the quarter and a 17 percent jump in operating income.
Smith Barney analyst Jill Krutick said a strong U.S. economy, good promotions in Florida and higher entrance prices during the quarter combined to push earnings higher.
Looking forward, she said bookings should remain strong throughout the summer.

For the six months, Disney reported net income of $1.1 billion, or $1.58 a share, up from $472 million, or 86 cents a share. The latest figures included a gain of $135 million from the sale of Los Angeles television station KCAL.
Revenues for the six-month period increased 8 percent to $11.8 billion and operating income expanded 24 percent to $2.3 billion.
